title: capacity-surge-scheduler-residual-state-postmortem
creator: Priya Raman
description: Summary: A production capacity surge on 2025-09-17 exposed a latent scheduler state retention bug which caused intermittent kernel-selection oscillation and elevated P95/P99 token latencies for routed requests. The incident lasted ~3.5 hours with elevated error budget burn for two enterprise customers on Dedicated pools. This ticket captures timeline, root cause analysis, mitigation steps taken during the event, and the consolidated action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2025-09-17T09:12Z - Alert: p95 token latency for region-us-west gateway crosses 300ms
2025-09-17T09:18Z - Oncall investigates: autoscaler added GPUs but latency persisted
2025-09-17T09:35Z - Observed frequent kernel probing logs and repeated kernel route reassignments across inference workers
2025-09-17T09:50Z - Partial mitigation: reduce probe concurrency and disable optimistic probe ramp for affected pools
2025-09-17T10:10Z - Latency trending down; cache warmup starts stabilizing tails
2025-09-17T12:50Z - Incident declared resolved for primary customers; full verification completed by 2025-09-17T13:00Z
root_cause: A change to scheduler speculative probing (merged in runtime-1.26) introduced a residual shared probe_state blob that was not reset on capacity rebalancing. When the autoscaler added GPUs during the surge, many workers concurrently issued kernel capability probes against newly created paths. The stale probe_state caused duplicated probe work and aggressive kernel reassignments leading to eviction of warmed KV caches and transient increases in sequence length workload mismatches. This produced higher per-token compute and queuing, manifesting as p95/p99 latency regressions.
impact:
- Affected: 2 enterprise Dedicated pools in us-west (customer A, customer B) and several hosted API accounts with burst traffic patterns
- Duration: ~3.5 hours of elevated error budget consumption
- Metrics: p95 generation latency +40-120ms; p99 +200-350ms; token cost per request increased by ~12% during peak
- Business: Customer-reported slowdowns for critical feature paths; support tickets opened by both customers
mitigations_applied_during_incident:
1) Reduced concurrent probe workers and disabled speculative probe ramp on affected pools (Diego M.).
2) Scoped autoscaler to avoid immediate mass attach across many racks; used staged attach policy (SRE lead: Maya K.).
3) Rolled back the speculative probe heuristic to last-known-stable in the runtime binary for critical pools (rollback PR: GH#r-infer/1762).
4) Increased KV cache retention window temporarily to avoid cold-start evictions.
action_items: AI-1: Add deterministic probe_state lifecycle — ensure probe_state is allocated per-attach and explicitly nulled on detach (owner: Diego) — due 2025-10-09
AI-2: Implement probe concurrency rate limiter with exponential backoff for probe failures and global probe ramp cap (owner: Priya) — due 2025-10-02
AI-3: Scheduler integration test: synthetic cluster test that simulates autoscaler attach/detach storms and asserts KV cache retention and stable kernel assignments (owner: Anton) — due 2025-10-16
AI-4: Monitoring: Add a composite SLI for 'probe-retry-rate' and 'route-churn-rate' with alert thresholds and runbook (owner: SRE oncall team) — due 2025-10-05
AI-5: Release gating: add canary gate to runtime rollout that verifies no more than 5% route churn in first 2 hours after deploy (owner: Release Eng) — due 2025-10-12
AI-6: PR audit: retroactive code review of runtime-1.26 speculative probe changes and create a short guidance doc for safe probe heuristics (owner: Priya & Diego) — due 2025-10-09
AI-7: Customer communication: Send post-incident summary to affected customers and propose a 1:1 architecture review (owner: CS lead, Maya) — due 2025-09-26 (completed)
AI-8: Update Runbook: include explicit steps for staged autoscaler attach and emergency rollback of probe heuristics (owner: SRE) — due 2025-10-01
